architecture_pattern.description: All input elements exist in the DOM as hidden modals. Event handlers are registered once when the page loads and remain active for the lifetime of the page. Modals simply toggle visibility via CSS classes.
benefits: Handlers work regardless of modal state
trade_offs: Handlers exist even when modals are closed (minimal memory impact)
Cannot dynamically change handler behavior without removing/re-adding

conclusion: NO ACTION REQUIRED. All keydown handlers are intentionally registered once at page load. This is a standard pattern for persistent DOM elements that toggle visibility. No memory leak exists.
